rows.note: Different season and a different quantity from rows pace-01 to pace-04, so it is a cross-check of them, not a second source for them. The reference resolver's live plays average 4.3 s, about 1 s short; the flow values are fitted to the snap-to-snap rows with that resolver and should be fitted again when it changes.

rows.statement: No-huddle share of college plays: 0.6. No source charts it. It is the mix of the pro huddle gap (pace-01) and the pro no-huddle gap (pace-02) that gives the college mean gap (pace-10): (38.84 - 33.27) / (38.84 - 29.87) = 0.62.

rows.note: The gate's target game.playsPerTeam is 66.1 from 2022 to 2025 pooled, which mixes the two clock rules.

rows.statement: The 40-second play clock starts when the play ends; the 25-second play clock starts with the referee's whistle.

sources.citation: 2026 NFL rulebook, Rule 4 Section 6 Articles 1 and 2

rows.statement: With the 40-second play clock running the ball is ready when an official places it; with the play clock set at 25 seconds it is ready, and the clock starts, when the referee sounds the whistle. The operator starts the 40-second clock within one second of the dead-ball signal.

sources.citation: 2026 NCAA football rule book, Rule 2 Section 2 Article 4 and Section 29 Article 2
